newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wage case ruling date remains unclear.
newsitem.headline: Australian wage case ruling date remains unclear.

text.p: The timing of a long-awaited decision by the Australian Industrial Relations Commission (AIRC) on the national "living wage" case remains unclear on Tuesday.
"I know nothing about any statement on timings, so I presume nothing's happened," a spokesman for employer group the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ACCI) told Reuters.
"It could come out anytime. We're expecting to get some notice," said a spokeswoman from peak union body the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU).
The AIRC said there would be no decision today.
Parties to the case are expected to be given 24 hours advanced warning of the AIRC ruling.
The trade union movement has claimed a rise in all award wage levels of A$20 a week plus 8.75 percent, and then two further A$20 rises over the next two years.
The ACCI has argued the Commission should reject the ACTU claim and begin work on simplification of award classifications.

The government, which has sought an A$8 weekly rise, has called the union claim irresponsible and the Reserve Bank has said the case could markedly affect Australia's ability to hold down inflation. -- Melbourne bureau 61-3 9286-1435
